subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Correction and reflection: giving kind and specific feedback
essential_question: How can understanding art and music around us help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for giving kind and specific feedback, then demonstrate corrected understanding.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of giving kind and specific feedback.
Check, revise, or improve work about giving kind and specific feedback using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about giving kind and specific feedback.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Critique and reflection work on giving kind and specific feedback. Critique and reflection: organize events, marks, sounds, words, objects, or movements through giving kind and specific feedback, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Try the first small step yourself; a grown-up may read or demonstrate on separate material.
primary_task: Target for this correct session: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for giving kind and specific feedback, then demonstrate corrected understanding. Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of giving kind and specific feedback. Check, revise, or improve work about giving kind and specific feedback using stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about giving kind and specific feedback; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. 1. Error analysis: Name the observable mismatch in earlier work without judging taste or effort. Locate it, compare it with the stated criterion, and choose the smallest useful repair. 2. Supported revision: Test the repair on a separate small study before changing the scored work. Use a different cue or representation and record what the test reveals. 3. Fresh transfer: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan. Record what the fresh evidence shows; keep the earlier attempt without penalty. Your choices remain yours: Different medium, subject or source material, sequence, criterion to test, final revision choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about giving kind and specific feedback. It is part of "Art and Music Around Us". Later days in this unit cover other things, like art and music in daily life. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about giving kind and specific feedback; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 3 you need one clear try with a grown-up nearby. Say or write your reason in a sentence or two. Drawings, objects, or spoken answers are all fine.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting giving kind and specific feedback.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce giving kind and specific feedback to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one sequence relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact sequence evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply giving kind and specific feedback under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on giving kind and specific feedback rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_registry.meaning: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one sequence relationship while working on giving kind and specific feedback.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.
Use a bounded study, loop, excerpt, map, or prototype to test one relationship without demanding polish.

age_policy.language: Short sections, one action at a time, and concrete noticing words.
age_policy.safety: Use familiar low-risk materials, stop or adjust any physical or sound action that causes discomfort, and require adult help for cutting, heat, fumes, or heavy equipment.
age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

concept_instruction.title: What giving kind and specific feedback means here
concept_instruction.body: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: Moving between media can reveal structure but may change the measured skill; name which evidence transfers and which does not. Worked example: Short → short-short → long can be drawn, tapped, moved, or silently counted while preserving its pattern of arrival, urgency, and rest. Non-example: Switching media and changing every relationship at once makes it impossible to tell what caused the new effect.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in giving kind and specific feedback.
technique_sequence.why: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for giving kind and specific feedback is present, but the record does not yet locate sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
